paper_title: Efficient and Accurate Group Testing via Belief Propagation: An Empirical Study
classifications: Mathematics of computing → Probabilistic inference problems
statement: What are the loose ends of the present work? On the one hand, it seems worthwhile to consider alternative noise models. A candidate might be one where the specificity decreases in the test size. Both the fixed noise model considered in this work and this diluted model have value from a practical perspective and it would be interesting to see whether our results carry over. On the other hand, the success of BP in practical group testing leaves us wondering whether it is guaranteed to converge to a fixpoint reminiscent of the ground truth. Hence, a mathematical analysis of BP remains as an outstanding open problem.
context: Apart from the group testing model studied in the present paper, there are complicated models; e.g., in quantitative group testing each test returns the number of infected samples rather than a binary positive or negative result.
